S1.why: Two words under the bracket; the tiles themselves show what is free.

S2.why: An invitation in the formal imperative the vocabulary uses for the person; fits every state, including nothing saved yet.

S3.s: Olete kasutanud kõik %lld tasuta cutlingit. Need jäävad tasuta ja töötavad ka edaspidi.
S3.back: (You) have used all 5 free cutling(partitive). They remain free and work also henceforth.
S3.why: Item word lowercased in running text as the vocabulary sentence does; partitive singular after the numeral.

S4.why: States the fact rather than 'you can save', and 'first' matches that these five stay free for good.

S5.why: Elative with a hyphen after the digit (5-st, 'out of five') is how Estonian writes it on screen.

S6.why: Noun line like the other bold rows; allative singular after the numeral reads 'room for'.

S7.why: Tekst and pilt are the vocabulary's own kind names, in partitive after the numbers.

S8.why: Estonian lists take no comma before 'ja'.

S9.s: Üks ost kehtib kõigis teie seadmetes sama Apple'i kontoga.
S9.back: One purchase is-valid in-all your devices same Apple's account-with.
S9.why: 'Apple'i konto' and lowercase 'teie' as in the vocabulary sentence; 'kehtib' is the word for a purchase or ticket being valid.

S10.why: The set phrase an Estonian reads on any receipt for a single payment.

S11.why: 'ega' carries the negation through the list, the native way to say 'no X, Y or Z'.

S12.why: The wording Estonian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action; singular imperative like Apple's buttons.

S13.why: Verbal noun as Apple uses for progress labels, with the ellipsis character.

S14.why: 'Avama' is the verb Estonian apps and games use for unlocking; 'eest' after the price is the plain 'for €x'. One-time is said in the row above.

S15.why: Same button without the price, so the words do not change when the price loads.

S16.why: Apple's Estonian wording for putting something off, which is not a refusal.

S17.why: The verb iOS uses on Estonian close buttons.

S18.why: Short, warm and a little proud; 'teie' alone as the possessive predicate.

S19.s: Aitäh, et toetate Cutlingit ja inimest, kes seda üksinda teeb.
S19.back: Thanks, that (you) support Cutling(partitive) and person(partitive), who it alone makes.
S19.why: 'Aitäh, et…' is the everyday Estonian thank-you; the one maker is named as a person, not a team.

S20.s: Tere tulemast tagasi. Teie varasem ost on taastatud.
S20.back: Welcome back. Your earlier purchase is restored.
S20.why: The standard greeting, then the fact with the same 'taasta' root as the link.

S21.s: Tasuta cutlinguid on %2$lld, neist on kasutatud %1$lld.
S21.back: Free cutlings(partitive-plural) are 5, of-them are used 3.
S21.why: Numbers stand where VoiceOver reads them in the nominative, so the speech keeps its case; positional forms because the order swaps.

S22.why: A count after a colon works for 1, 2, 5 and 21 without a plural form, and 'mahub kuni' keeps the big number nominative when spoken.

S23.s: Täisversioon on kasutusel. Nüüd mahub %@ cutlingit.
S23.back: Full-version is in-use. Now fits 5 000 cutling(partitive).
S23.why: 'Täisversioon' is the one name for the unlocked app across sheet, Siri and Mac; numeral plus partitive reads correctly aloud.

S24.why: Says what happened with no one at fault.

S25.s: App Store'iga ei saa praegu ühendust. Proovige mõne aja pärast uuesti.
S25.back: App Store-with not get now connection. Try(you-formal) some time after again.
S25.why: Apostrophe before the case ending because 'Store' ends in a silent e; formal imperative for the retry.

S26.s: App Store ei kinnitanud seda ostu.
S26.back: App Store not confirmed this purchase(partitive).
S26.why: Plain past tense, partitive object after the negation.

S27.s: Selles seadmes sisse logitud Apple'i kontol pole varasemat Cutlingi ostu.
S27.back: In-this device signed-in Apple's account-on isn't earlier Cutling's purchase.
S27.why: 'Sisse logima' and 'Apple'i konto' as in the vocabulary sentence.

S28.s: Tasuta versioon mahutab %lld cutlingit. Ühe ostuga saate salvestada nii palju, kui soovite.
S28.back: Free version holds 5 cutling(partitive). One purchase-with (you) can save as much, as (you) wish.
S28.why: 'Tasuta versioon' pairs with 'täisversioon'; the comma before 'kui' is required.

S29.why: A compact number pair under the title, which already names the list.

K1.s: %lld tasuta kohta on täis – avage kõik
K1.back: 5 free place(partitive) are full – unlock(you-formal) all
K1.why: 'Koht' is the slot, not the item; the en dash with spaces is the Estonian dash; 'avage kõik' matches the sheet's button. 35 characters.

M1.why: A verb-led command name like Estonian Mac window and menu titles (Ava…, Salvesta…).

M2.why: The same command as the window, with the ellipsis because it opens a window.

M3.why: A row label is a noun phrase; capitalized only because it starts the label.

M4.why: The compact pair used in Estonian settings rows.

M5.why: Status phrasing without a verb, as settings values are; 22 characters.

M6.s: Üks ost avab täisversiooni iPhone'is, iPadis ja Macis.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks full-version(genitive) iPhone-in, iPad-in and Mac-in.
M6.why: Inessive endings on the device names, apostrophe only after the silent e of iPhone.

M7.s: Täisversioon on kasutusel iPhone'is, iPadis ja Macis selle Apple'i kontoga.
M7.back: Full-version is in-use iPhone-in, iPad-in and Mac-in this Apple's account-with.
M7.why: Same status words as M5, so the bought state has one name.

M8.s: Ostsite Cutlingi, kui see oli veel tasuline, seega jääb täisversioon teile. Aitäh.
M8.back: (You) bought Cutling(genitive), when it was still paid, so stays full-version to-you. Thanks.
M8.why: 'Tasuline' (paid) avoids 'sai tasuta', which would read as 'got it for free'; thanks closes the line.
